analysis_steps.goal: Select unblended optically thin CH3OD lines

method.value: Remove blended and optically thick lines (tau>0.1 at Tex 50 or 300 K, N=4.5e16) from 485 covered lines, leaving 97 unique frequencies

evidence.quote: After the removal of the blended and optically thick lines, $97$ unique line frequencies remained

analysis_steps.goal: Fit LTE synthetic spectra for Tex and N

method.value: MCMC fit of LTE synthetic spectra including non-detected lines

evidence.quote: The fitting methodology is based on the MCMC Python package EMCEE

key_parameters.value: Beam and source size fixed to 0.5"; FWHM 1 km/s; vLSR 2.7 km/s; 300 walkers; 1500 steps for joint fit

evidence.quote: Beam size and source size were both fixed to $0.5''$ and were both assumed to have Gaussian distributions
assume that the excitation of the molecule is characterized by local thermodynamical equilibrium (LTE)
the mean acceptance fraction of the $300$ walkers is $70-71\%$

validation.value: Corner plot convergence; compared with old spectroscopy

evidence.quote: the quality of the convergence is illustrated in the corner plot

analysis_steps.goal: Derive D/H of methanol hydroxy group

evidence.quote: the statistical correction on the D/H ratio for the case of deuteration in the hydroxy group is one
The fitting methodology is based on the MCMC Python package EMCEE

used_for.value: Fitting torsion-rotation Hamiltonian and predicting CH3OD line list

evidence.quote: We employed the RAM36 code (cite: Ilyushin:2010; Ilyushin:2013)
The newly determined best-fitting D/H ratio for CH$_{3}$OD is $(0.32\pm0.09)\%$.
A Hamiltonian model consisting of 134 parameters provided a fit with a weighted root mean square (wrms) deviation of 0.85

findings_qualitative.value: Hydroxy-group D/H is ~7.5 times lower than methyl-group D/H, the lowest of measured molecules in IRAS 16293B

evidence.quote: the newly determined hydroxy group deuteration is a factor of $\sim$7.5 lower

claims.hypothesis: Do new spectroscopy change CH3OD N and Tex toward IRAS 16293B?
claims.experiment: LTE MCMC fit of 97 lines in PILS using new line list
claims.result: N=3.25e16 cm-2, Tex=190 K; N lower by ~5.5
claims.finding: Earlier column density was overestimated, partly due to a partition function factor-of-four error

evidence.quote: which corresponds to a reduction by a factor of $\sim$5.5 in $N$ and $\sim$1.6 in $T_{\text{ex}}$

claims.hypothesis: Does OD D/H match CH3 D/H in methanol?
claims.experiment: Compare new D/H with earlier methyl value

evidence.quote: this implies that the D/H ratio in the hydroxy group of methanol does not match the D/H ratio in the methyl group of methanol

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Fitting v_t=0 and 1 separately judged unnecessary

evidence.quote: there is no reason to fit the $\varv_{\rm t}=0$ and $1$ states of CH$_{3}$OD separately in the PILS data

limitations_admitted.value: Temperature/column gradients and compact emission of high-excitation lines may bias fit; no higher resolution constraints

evidence.quote: it is likely that there are gradients in temperatures, column densities, and extents of the emission along the line of sight

referee_caveats_inferred: Errors on N and Tex are assumed 20% and 10%, not MCMC-derived
Single-component LTE with fixed 0.5" source size
D/H depends on adopted methanol column from earlier work
